#
If you’ve followed my campaign for long, you know that **I _love_ coffee — especially from Wawa!** And probably a little too much, if I’m being honest. 😬
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mcb-em-20250213-1?refcode=em20250213-1755&amount=5&refcode2=1755_21716_TpzArf&akid=1755%2E21716%2ETpzArf)
So while I’m taking a quick coffee break between meetings on Capitol Hill, I wanted to send you a quick note to ask for your help on something important.
We’re closing in on our February mid-month deadline, and with everything going on right now, we need to reach all of our fundraising goals. Republicans and the media will be looking to Democratic fundraising as a gauge of the national mood, and we need to make sure those numbers reflect how upset people are right now.
Because even though people _do_ ask me about my Wawa order, more often they’re asking me what we’re doing to hold the Trump administration accountable, bring down the cost of housing and groceries, make childcare more affordable, and make sure everyone has paid medical leave.
**These are the issues Delawareans elected me to fight for, and I’m committed to working nonstop to get the job done. No matter how many coffee runs it takes!**
[**If you’re with me, will you pitch in $5 or more before our big mid-month deadline on 2/15? ## SB25-047: A Step Towards a Safer Colorado
|
---
Yesterday, John Fabbricatore joined Douglas County Sheriff Darren Weekly, Senator Mark Baisley and Rep. Max Brooks to discuss the county’s support for **SB25-047 (Enforcement of Federal Immigration Law).** “This bill helps the citizens of this state - the legal residents of this state. Sanctuary law does not protect our citizens. It protects criminal illegal aliens and **this bill will ensure we have the cooperation between local law enforcement and federal law enforcement that is needed to keep communities safe.”** SAFE Colorado fully supports this effort to start to roll back our sanctuary policies and put us in the right direction. With your help, we can work to push this common-sense legislation gets over the finish line. Sign our pledge at [www.safecolorado.org](https://rpgdxp.clicks.mlsend.com/tl/cl/eyJ2Ijoie1wiYVwiOjEyOTI0MjMsXCJsXCI6MTQ2MjcxNTM1ODEzODg3MDYzLFwiclwiOjE0NjI3MTU0Njk0MDMyNzI0OH0iLCJzIjoiNWRlMDAxMjg1YmQwOGMwOSJ9) and come out to **_testify in support of SB25-047 on February 25th at 2pm_** in the Senate State, Military & Veterans Affairs Committee.

body:
This week, I launched my campaign for Governor of the great state of New Mexico.
[](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/85830?refcode=em20250213-8768&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=8768%2E614464%2EpetLaj)
Heartland Patriots said I could reach out with some exciting news, Peter:
This week, I launched my campaign for Governor of the great state of New Mexico — my home — to bring our state together and build a bright future for all who live here.
I’m humbly asking: **[Will you join us by donating just $3 or more to my campaign and Heartland Patriots now?](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/85830?refcode=em20250213-8768&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=8768%2E614464%2EpetLaj)**
The amount you give doesn’t matter. What matters is building a campaign with the support of real people. That’s who I am and who I came from. That’s who I am running to serve.
My roots in New Mexico run 35 generations deep. The Pueblo people were the first farmers in the high deserts of New Mexico, an agriculture tradition that still continues today.
I am here because of my grandfather, who worked for decades as a diesel mechanic on the railroad. Somehow he also kept a field — picking worms off the corn as it grew, like the generations before him.
I am here because of my grandmother, a survivor and a caretaker who woke up every day before the sun. She was the one who gave me my true love of cooking New Mexican cuisine. (She wouldn’t let us in the kitchen while she cooked, but I’d perch myself outside and watch her through the window for hours.)
I am here because of my parents and their sacrifice. My mother, a Pueblo woman, served in the Navy. My father, a Marine, received a Silver Star for his service in Vietnam. He now lies in honor at Arlington.
I am here because of my beloved child, who I raised on my own. I started a small business to pay the bills, but it still wasn’t always enough. We relied on food stamps to get on our feet. I sometimes had to decide between paying rent and buying groceries to feed our family. I will never forget how that felt or the kindness of those who helped us – strangers who became community. When I look at my Somah, I see perseverance, strength and hope.
These are my stories.
These are stories of New Mexico.
These days, our differences are blown so far out of proportion. We lose sight of a simple fact: we all live in the same state, together. All of us in New Mexico come from love, survival, and sacrifice. We all want to live good lives — and we want even more for our children.
The current president and his billionaire friends look at the lands and the people of this country and think: what can I exploit?
I am running to ask: if we come together in New Mexico, what good can we do for each other and for the next generation?
We have our work cut out for us. The cost of living is crushing our families. Our economy is growing, but we need to make sure everyone shares in our progress. Our families need more. Our farmers and ranchers need more. New Mexico’s children need so much more. And we must be good stewards of the Earth, and preserve the rivers, mesas, farmlands, and forests whose beauty sustains our communities.
I am running to do all this and more. I am running to serve all New Mexicans and make sure we’re leaving a better future for our children.

I would be honored to have your support.](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/85830?refcode=em20250213-8768&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=8768%2E614464%2EpetLaj)**

Be fierce,
Deb

I am here because of my grandmother, a survivor and a caretaker who woke up every day before the sun. She was the one who gave me my true love of cooking New Mexican cuisine. body:
please read this update

Friend, last month I said our goal for January was to make it our best January yet.

Thanks to the support of folks like you, that's exactly what we did. _**[The NRSC had its best off-year January ever.](http://e.americanbriefing.com/rd/9z2zmhofoqj91qnqn4fvs04bda708tr65le88sn7o10_rp22sh2s8i6epj4slj6apj4c5h2bs)**_

That kind of early fundraising now is what will make the difference in a tough fight to defend Senate seats and grow our majority next year.

We have to defend seats across the country, from North Carolina to Ohio. And we must seize our opportunities to flip seats in places like Michigan and Georgia.

With your help, we can achieve all of it.

_**[An investment now is an investment in Republican wins and a four-year majority for President Trump, so please kick in a few bucks if you can.](http://e.americanbriefing.com/rd/9z2zv9meguji8qpstrgrvj1ss1k2jcui4f0ktghomp8_rp22sh2s8i6epj4slj6apj4c5h2bs)**_

Thank you for your steadfast support.

---
Are you loving President Trump’s Department of Government Efficiency? Because I certainly am.

_Thanks to Elon Musk’s audit of the federal government, the American public is finally learning the full extent of the government’s corruption, waste, and inefficiency._

_...The _TRUTH_._
---

---
_The same political party that hired 80,000 IRS agents to target hardworking taxpaying citizens is now terrified that YOU are finally getting access to the uncensored truth._
---
_Look, President Trump and I both ran on a promise to drain the swamp. But when you drain a swamp, you see, for the very first time, all the venomous creatures that had been lurking at the bottom._
---
And that’s what’s happening right now: The more that gets exposed, the more the Democrats will fight us tooth and nail.
---
**But so long as President Trump and I have the FULL BACKING of the AMERICAN PEOPLE, we will prevail against any attack the Democrats throw at us.**

And savvy grassroots activists like you know, just like we do, that we can’t stop watching the people we help elect: after the elections, we have to keep organizing support for the policies we like and pushing back against the ones we don’t. When the public tunes out between elections and the only people our elected officials hear from are the paid lobbyists of wealthy corporations, our government stops being accountable to the needs of ordinary families. Democracy never sleeps, and neither can we. So we ask that you support our work, so we can continue to engage in this fight every moment of every day. So our kids grow up in democracy, not dystopia. Thank you for your support for all we do! Please follow Cliff Schecter on Twitter @cliffschecter, or subscribe to The Takedown with Cliff Schecter on YouTube, to keep up to date with this battle for the heart and soul of our country. — You're getting this message because you’ve supported good causes and Democratic candidates. We need your support to continue fighting for our democracy. We love having you in our network, but if you no longer wish to hear from us, you can._ | Paid for by Blue Amp Action PAC | | or

name: Office of U.S. Senator Angela Alsobrooks
subject: Senator Alsobrooks Newsletter -- February 14
body:
|
---
Friends and neighbors:
It's been a busy week on Capitol Hill and across Maryland. From rallies to floor speeches to telephone town halls, I've been working with my colleagues, union members, and Marylanders to push back against the Trump/Musk Administration. Just yesterday we saw this Administration continue to purge federal civil servants. This callous and cruel witch hunt isn't about making government more efficient. It's about enacting this President's retribution on civil servants and the people they serve - the American people. It's a disgraceful series of actions meant to upend American lives, cut American jobs, and destroy the American spirit that calls so many of us to serve in this way. As you probably also know, a federal judge in Boston lifted the pause on the "Fork in the Road" deferred resignation program for federal employees. The Trump Administration quickly declared victory, but I would like to be clear on what occurred here. The suit was decided on the grounds that the unions filing the suit could not prove they would be harmed by the President and Elon Musk's actions. It did not get to the actual legal question of whether or not it was lawful to put civil servants in a situation where they were forced to make that decision. I will continue to monitor the mounting legal cases against this Administration in their clear disregard for the rule of law and the Constitution that binds our nation together. We also have a responsibility right now to leverage the court of public opinion. This Administration needs to understand the dire impacts its reckless actions will have on the American people. When you attack civil servants, you are attacking the people they serve - the American people. It is paramount that Republican representatives hear from the people being impacted by these cuts in funding and personnel. These are trying times, no doubt. But the spirit of Maryland has always been one of resilience. Together, we will not only push back, but push forward. Let's take a look at the past week: **17,000 People Joined Our Telephone Town Hall** Senator Chris Van Hollen and I hosted a telephone town hall with featured speaker, Rob Shriver, the former Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Acting Director who is leading the effort at Democracy Forward to protect our civil servants. 17,000 of you tuned in. We heard questions from Marylanders across the state on everything from the threats Elon Musk poses to our personal data to the way this Administration is targeting Maryland jobs. A Vietnam war veteran was concerned about his retirement benefits; another woman was let go from her job and didn't know what to do next. We heard from seniors on Medicare who are worried about Republicans rolling back the Inflation Reduction Act, which allows Medicare to negotiate directly with pharmaceutical companies and capped the cost of lifesaving medications for seniors - they were concerned they will no longer be able to afford their medication. My office door is always open. Please continue to reach out and share your stories. It is testimony we can use as we push back using every legislative tool at our disposal. I also want to say to those who feel they have been wrongly fired from their civil servant job you can visit [https://www.democrats.senate.gov/whistleblowers](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=14120.5407216.5043432.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.democrats.senate.gov%2fwhistleblowers&redir_log=534139256143340) to submit a whistleblower complaint. **Pushing Back Against The Trump/Musk Administration** I opened this letter highlighting the importance of the court of public opinion. Here's some of what we accomplished this week: On Monday, I joined Senator Chris Van Hollen, Representatives Kweisi Mfume, Johnny Olszewski, and Sarah Elfreth, AFGE National Vice President Jason Anderson and dozens of concerned Marylanders for a [rally outside the Social Security Administration](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=14120.5407216.5043432.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fx.com%2fSen_Alsobrooks%2fstatus%2f1889021534745796699&redir_log=817114256253334) Headquarters in Woodlawn. Thousands of Marylanders have been coming to work at the Social Security building in Woodlawn for over 60 years now. They are doing the essential work of processing and issuing Social Security checks to nearly 72 million Americans. It is work they have done under Democratic Presidents. And it is work they have done under Republican Presidents. And now, 60 years later, the people who work in this building are being callously and shamefully targeted in the President's witch hunt for federal workers. In his hunt for vengeance, the President has decided that no target is too small, no family too vulnerable, no American out of bounds. What's more is that it is becoming increasingly clear (not that there ever was any doubt) that Elon Musk has no interest whatsoever in making the government more efficient. He's cutting jobs. He's cutting funding for cancer research. And he's busy accessing Americans' private data. It's shameful.
On Tuesday, I joined AFGE President Everette Kelley, and hundreds of union workers - from AFGE, SEIU, AFSCME, ATU, APWU and more - for a [rally outside the U.S. Capitol](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=14120.5407216.5043432.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fx.com%2fSen_Alsobrooks%2fstatus%2f1889377262069485922&redir_log=231207398234334), to continue making the point that an attack on the federal workers in Maryland is a direct attack on the American people they serve. The exhausted mother, who calls the 9-8-8 lifeline for support on the darkest of days... The single dad who has to call out of work because his daughter's Head Start classroom closed its doors... The family business that didn't get their disaster relief check to rebuild after the flood waters receded... The grandmother stretching her fixed income to feed a nourishing meal to her grandkids, turned away at the checkout line when her SNAP EBT card declines... The woman seeking refuge from an abusive partner, just to be turned away from the local family violence shelter... The first generation college student that loses their Pell grant and Federal Work Study, and can't afford to stay in school... The veteran whose appointment at the VA gets cancelled, delaying his screening and treatment from his battlefield exposure. These are the Americans our civil servants have spent their lives serving. And I'm going to do everything in my power to make sure they can keep doing that essential service.
**Holding the Floor to Delay Robert F. Kennedy Jr. Confirmation** This week, I worked with my colleagues to hold the Senate Floor up over the nomination of Robert F. Kennedy Jr. to serve as the Secretary of Health and Human Services. I had the opportunity to question Mr. Kennedy. His answers [were deeply concerning](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=14120.5407216.5043432.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fx.com%2fSen_Alsobrooks%2fstatus%2f1885036716928483424&redir_log=644271641036333). This is not a man seeking scientific consensus but rather a man obsessed with conspiracy. This is not a man who has studied medicine or scientific research at NIH (he will support the Trump cuts) but rather a man who has dedicated his life to promoting anti-vaccine propaganda. This is not a man who has any business leading the Department of Health and Human Services. I spoke forcefully against his nomination on the Floor. And this week in a hearing, [I asked Dr. Verdin](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=14120.5407216.5043432.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fx.com%2fSen_Alsobrooks%2fstatus%2f1889806835416441199&redir_log=026196575777334), the President/CEO of the Buck Institute for Research on Aging, about the importance of NIH funding. Dr Verdin was unequivocal: the NIH is the crown jewel of all biomedical research organizations in the world. Robert F. Kennedy Jr. was confirmed yesterday. But this fight is not over. I will continue to use the bully pulpit to push back against this dangerous quackery he continues to peddle. **Conclusion** Amidst all the chaos this week, all caused by the Trump Administration, we learned that costs are going up. In fact, [inflation is speeding up](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=14120.5407216.5043432.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fx.com%2fSen_Alsobrooks%2fstatus%2f1889753116691612011&redir_log=518420540681332). Instead of putting forth nominees like Robert F. Kennedy Jr. or trying to gut the federal workforce, this President needs to be focused on getting our costs down. My office is open to any leader -- regardless of Party -- who wants to focus on lowering costs for hardworking Marylanders. When this Administration is ready to stop this witch hunt for Maryland workers, when they are ready to stop toeing the line for this President, when they are ready to stop causing harm to Americans by gutting federal programs, I will be here ready to have a serious conversation about making lives better. Until then, I will continue to oppose this Administration on the Senate Floor, in communities across Maryland -- and everywhere in the court of public opinion. And I know I am not in this fight alone. Between our telephone town hall and rallies, I have seen so many of you organizing, pushing back, and standing up for Maryland values. Each and every day it is a profound privilege to do this work on behalf of the people of our great state. I also want to wish everyone a beautiful and loving Valentine's Day. Please encourage your friends and neighbors to sign up for our newsletter by going to our website [www.alsobrooks.senate.gov](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=14120.5407216.5043432.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.alsobrooks.senate.gov%2f&redir_log=992708218041239). It's one of the best ways to stay informed. Please also follow me on social media at @sen_alsobrooks on X, Instagram, Facebook, and Threads. Sincerely, Angela Alsobrooks
United States Senator

| Dear Hello Happy Valentine's Day.
I had no idea what a big deal Valentine's Day was until my first year in the Virginia Senate. It's an annual tradition that each legislative office decorate their office for Valentines' Day. It's a sight to see. In fact, I've never seen anything like it since then.
If you've been putting off that trip to visit your General Assembly, be sure to go on Valentine's Day. With Valentine's Day falling on a Friday, it will be a festive fun day as legislative work winds down for the year.
That said, there are a number of controversial bills being debated on the Virginia Senate floor tomorrow, to include a number of House patroned "gun grabbing" bills. Please tune in.
Also, please click on each of the committee above for the full listing of all bills coming up on Friday, along with the bill title, sponsor and description. Too many to list today. Please review thoroughly.

## RFK Jr. Sworn In as Health Secretary
[Robert F. Kennedy Jr. was sworn in](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJx0kLGO6yAQRb_G7hzBzBBwQfGadHntltZghphdHFuYTZS_X2X7La-udHR0Pq7TlXPJ99t_XsW3tE2gwAwKBk1T5FxeE_XRJxEQ7MVri6NBNKT6xbvkkIOxI0IwIYhOiNqNzhKjKOY--zdNgSatyYA7RUo0ElqegzImhI6UxNy2evrc8r0tkspre0g9zdvaF7-0th8d_uvg0sGF97s8j_f1HrXluUgHl5q-hla_131YhEtbhkPmKo3ra3hsTQYTgySRpAzaOANpOaeAGFwCtuRCX33cn7mUfJxtR-q2ci6_Au2vIA8PPwEAAP__7eFiHw) Thursday as President Trump's health secretary after a 52-48 Senate vote and is set to take control of the $1.7 trillion Health and Human Services Department, overseeing vaccine policy, health insurance programs, and food safety. Senate Minority Leader Mitch McConnell was the lone Republican to oppose Kennedy, citing Kennedy's views on vaccines. In other confirmation news, [Kash Patel, the nominee for FBI director](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJx0kD2P4jAQQH-N0xn5M4HCxTXpuPbKaGKP8XB2jJJZEP9-xfZbP-k96f27LlegStvtLzQMnPtilPFSGandkoDqe3FDChnRoB0w6MlevLXeqaGEEfV4gRHzatd4niCnrHCM0Z_XCdzkBwofmzLaae28OZ-Sy-7i7ARxVd6vq3AKE3HfT_dOGxfM9d2fuJ9ib0MNhflxCPtHmFmYmQsWqvXDhJlLb7jh6xBmhtRoo4N3YOqbMLPXVmk3yf9wFPkAxioP3IBR3r8SRYL9LWNvjZgR5bMzCjMPe0iPF9VKxzgJp24N6Cc28G9jnsF8BwAA__8etmb8), cleared a Senate panel in a party-line vote Thursday, setting up a final confirmation vote next week. # Time to celebrate...or not: Valentines and Presidents
---
We have two national holidays upon us - Valentine’s Day (Feb 14) and Presidents Day (Feb 17) and we wanted to reflect on what that means given current affairs. [The History of Valentine’s Day](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMUnD7bJeyjZeK4yJZBznDoEf0StXH8h1WQY-d-FSz7uEvsJ7pP3HxllLj2FaXQvqlQjwc5LsApw-hQtSIDKOdaueZiIRIodBD3YP42z1HQHrlvnnLRpZGwiYafpDLDERKgFoCzvAzQCuMj6_8Iq9F79SPpfzvRp-q7Iyp2qoBVnKc2UuAh53rl7skKtl9JrlWdBU8_zp4FVFnRY95pkbtFRc1Qozz0DmT9ckogF3d9KzTA93y34UTIaau_PWcjHgybCR83DU7SnzC5z4E6NJX7mZ4g2Ck-I69kieUsW1n7lr3BI9X2uMI0F-yBAdP5fpX8f_7jCbfxdhWBv1I3Wa3vl3FOeMfRu6-vfY8nH9nmFPx80AYGb-6AwHzz6TavERaA/4e0/7YTe5OiXT125xDPFtqXJUQ/h1/h001.N6_BEb2xseU3EUi2cWKFP6xxTquBCJnMjZ0HQpQV0Wo) is kind of interesting. Valentine (whichever version you like) was a rebel—he defied and stood up for love and injustice. While most people associate this day with cupid, flowers, chocolate and hearts - there are some other pretty notable things have occurred on this day:
* Valentine’s Day Massacre - 1928 Chicago
* Captain James Cook is killed after kidnapping King Kalaniopuu - 1779, Hawaii
* Oregon becomes a state - 1859
* Battle of Kettle Creek, one of the most consequential battles during the American Revolution - Georgia, 1779
* Alexander Graham Bell applies for his first patent for a telephone - 1876
* Arizona becomes a state - 1912
* Jimmy Hoffa is born - 1913, Indiana
* Bombing of Dresden - 1945, Germany

Monday, February 17th is Presidents Day (or Washington’s birthday). It's not lost on us that we will celebrate the birthday of our very first President who led the fight against a tyrannical monarchy so we could build a democracy while our current president (and his administration) are working to gain the unchecked power of a monarchy and dismantle democracy. George Washington (and all our founding mother’s and father’s) would be appalled and, we imagine, back to organizing a revolution!

# Blocking disability access at schools and hospitals? Silencing ADA challenges? NO WAY!
---
The hits against people with disabilities just keep coming and everyone should know what’s going on. As a part of Pres. Trump ending so-called Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Accessibility (DEI) policies, a memo was sent to the Justice Department's Civil Rights Division to not file any new complaints. As KPEF’s Disability Justice Program Director, Mallory Hudson, explained to [Public News Service](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMQJLJbRUAuUzE4jICamY2RmHZ9ODLSIJjQtTJaLLJdPrRyguOEn2Llng92kQQevxhW8m9L3KUDUAOcevaZpvOdST712SQIw-e09NwrTKA3Bl4ebUD3R1Af92IU8_VOOfhaunFgakTywcRK11o-pyafhP5f1QxU_VqQNDY0lcB8tfIb_NxPICHxD5EMONGjMrSrT4Cm68U7qWck2lcyI60xv_fWRBPc-wyqDau-nlGGwcI9NRxwJGANpB_hD5l4DNYiw6OuC5krQW7hKziB-udfHkm-lcZU1MsT5WcTYQpVVMpfhHtWc5ULj0v7rbGiLRzRIJPI3RQPosukOgMb2JS4cdtDQNcm0imnnUIZeacoT3cOqLbeyJhET0mQ8ATVVGDuE5Y01VIJXeQbbZhK_keV4be2LVJUfTIyC5OfKB_Dyv9SAGi5IXVAEABMJ2s-uN0g/4e0/7YTe5OiXT125xDPFtqXJUQ/h2/h001.1vQJsXFQYgAS7_VN7-_-7URtd1kbzNImApK-aZCb3Zg), “That means that the **Department of Justice Civil Rights Division has been instructed not to file any new civil rights cases, right?** " said Hudson. "And that includes ADA complaints. So, those are - **that is one of the few ways that disabled people can even protect their civil rights.”**

name: History Facts
subject: Did the Romans celebrate Valentine's Day?
body:
It’s often speculated that Valentine’s Day has its roots in the ancient Roman festival of Lupercalia, and it’s not hard to see why. [](https://track.historyfacts.com/?xtl=1krv9cfc68dov67sjhbxlxj71mr5o46w0fylm8s6cqskskb7fj2o6ptwsofw2x69g3lyhaxemt9usa8vba6zrwq0pay10lde2ayajhxnfqi7vfjiqklpklauwbf46j1wnlny4lgotuul56ttppdtw7q5r&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=sro9lj&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com)
---
---
# [Ancient Romans celebrated a fertility holiday on February 15.](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=sro9lj&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com)
### [World History](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=sro9lj&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com)
[](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=sro9lj&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com)
| I t’s often speculated that Valentine’s Day has its roots in the ancient Roman festival of [Lupercalia](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=sro9lj&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com), and it’s not hard to see why. Lupercalia was observed on February 15, and involved fertility rituals — albeit along with animal sacrifice and ritual whipping. Yet the link between this pagan festival and the Christian feast day that morphed into our modern ode to love and romance is murky, and indeed may be little more than coincidence.**** At its peak, Lupercalia — which dates back to at least the sixth century BCE, predating Christianity by centuries — was a really wild time. A group of nude Roman priests kicked off the events in [Lupercal Cave](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=sro9lj&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com) at the bottom of Palatine Hill with the sacrifice of a dog and at least one goat. They painted themselves in the blood and wiped it off their skin with milk-soaked wool, then cut strips of goat hide and whipped women on the hands with them to promote fertility.
---
As time went on, Lupercalia mellowed out, and the nudity dramatically subsided. Yet it was still too much for Pope Gelasius I, who forbade participation in the festival at the end of the fifth century CE. One common theory is that he supplanted the pagan festival with St. Valentine’s Day, also known as the Feast of St. Valentine, though [recent historians](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=sro9lj&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com) have shed doubt on that claim. For one thing, St. Valentine, a third-century Christian martyr, had no connection to love or romance. In fact, the holiday didn’t get its modern association until Geoffrey Chaucer wrote a poem linking St. Valentine’s Day and mating season in the 14th century, some 900 years after the holiday was established.
[](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=sro9lj&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com) | [](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=sro9lj&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com)

## Conversation hearts used to have much longer messages.
Tiny boxes of candy hearts emblazoned with short phrases such as “BE MINE” and “LOVE YOU” are ubiquitous on Valentine’s Day. But when these now-iconic candies first hit the market, they were a little bigger and a [lot wordier](https://track.historyfacts.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=sro9lj&__onlt=h&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com). Necco started selling the chalky confections in 1847, and in 1866 devised a way to print letters on them in vegetable ink. The early drafts were not as catchy, and included such phrases as “Married in white, you have chosen right,” “Married in pink, he’ll take to drink,” and the extra-lengthy “How long shall I have to wait? Please be considerate.”

clean_body: It’s often speculated that Valentine’s Day has its roots in the ancient Roman festival of Lupercalia, and it’s not hard to see why. | I t’s often speculated that Valentine’s Day has its roots in the ancient Roman festival of , and it’s not hard to see why. Lupercalia was observed on February 15, and involved fertility rituals — albeit along with animal sacrifice and ritual whipping. Yet the link between this pagan festival and the Christian feast day that morphed into our modern ode to love and romance is murky, and indeed may be little more than coincidence.**** At its peak, Lupercalia — which dates back to at least the sixth century BCE, predating Christianity by centuries — was a really wild time. A group of nude Roman priests kicked off the events in at the bottom of Palatine Hill with the sacrifice of a dog and at least one goat. They painted themselves in the blood and wiped it off their skin with milk-soaked wool, then cut strips of goat hide and whipped women on the hands with them to promote fertility. As time went on, Lupercalia mellowed out, and the nudity dramatically subsided. Yet it was still too much for Pope Gelasius I, who forbade participation in the festival at the end of the fifth century CE. One common theory is that he supplanted the pagan festival with St. Valentine’s Day, also known as the Feast of St. Valentine, though have shed doubt on that claim. For one thing, St. Valentine, a third-century Christian martyr, had no connection to love or romance. In fact, the holiday didn’t get its modern association until Geoffrey Chaucer wrote a poem linking St. Valentine’s Day and mating season in the 14th century, some 900 years after the holiday was established. | Thank you for supporting our advertisers! | By the Numbers | | Visitors to the archaeological park that includes Palatine Hill in 2023 12 million | | Years of Gelasius I’s papacy 4 | Years of Gelasius I’s papacy 4 | | Population of Valentine, Texas 73 | | Year Constantine I legalized Christianity in the Roman Empire 313 CE | Year Constantine I legalized Christianity in the Roman Empire 313 CE | | | Did you know? ---|---|--- Conversation hearts used to have much longer messages. Tiny boxes of candy hearts emblazoned with short phrases such as “BE MINE” and “LOVE YOU” are ubiquitous on Valentine’s Day. But when these now-iconic candies first hit the market, they were a little bigger and a . Necco started selling the chalky confections in 1847, and in 1866 devised a way to print letters on them in vegetable ink. The early drafts were not as catchy, and included such phrases as “Married in white, you have chosen right,” “Married in pink, he’ll take to drink,” and the extra-lengthy “How long shall I have to wait? ## Burrows Announces House Committee Assignments
Speaker Dustin Burrows (R-Lubbock) [announced committee assignments](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx0kL2OgzAQhJ_GdEb2YsAULq6hy7VXIoOXYMU_CG9C8vanpLnq2hl9o9H3c5ku1gefrt82oqHnmicQ0HIBXKrJWR9ek6qcmYUbZIVG9s3QNp0SutqMW4e1abVDKYTuZo1923aim50YNMpFVt68xwRIJQF6JWu7DFZpgK4Ht-oZmBLoPOWjpg0Jn7as4ZUfeNRLjlUwG9FeWPPFYGQwnudZ3542vUsGY8KzMBg_GN9z8OSXv6DsaG948Lxy2pBv-V6Q25TyPS1Y-JJj9ESI3JbiryliojdcHcbtpw_Bl65nSlyj9eHzhv7V8zDwGwAA__-ER2n8) for the Texas House yesterday, keeping his promise to appoint Republicans as chairs of all standing committees and Democrats as vice chairs. Republicans also have a majority in each committee of the GOP-controlled chamber. However, Democrats were appointed to chair six of twelve subcommittees, and Democrat Joe Moody of El Paso was [named the speaker pro tempore](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx0kL9uwyAchJ8GNiP4mfBnYIgqeUuHLh0tMGAjQbACjZO3rxKpY8fTne6Tvu_LfLEpp-v6aUsw_RHrDBROA4WB8dnblJ8zx9446jXDwTA56tMoOFV4M0wLEZkbY4TgFI8Ll9oxzayQIxWgcDKvMwqMMwDJGbGLtlwBCAk-KgeI0-BTrzfSt9DDw7aYn_UebmSpBWez9b43NJ4RTAim4zjIVn9aIO8pWesdwbT72BBMSy0l9R7CKyj9NZxbS-u1hGtvg3sOH3892X3EN-P3I-WcmpCI07XYlN_M_q-Eu4HfAAAA__-bH19w). Most chairmanships were awarded to veteran legislators who backed Burrows in his bid for speaker rather than the GOP caucus nominee, Rep. David Cook of Mansfield, who was [appointed to lead the Subcommittee on Juvenile Justice](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx00L2uozAQBeCngc7IHhx-Chdp6O4W22yJJvYAozXYsp1ws0-_Iv2tZqQjfTo6f77mL2TPx_oLdzLlewkzSLgJCULp2SH796xrZx7Sjaomo_p2vLWdlkO9GQKJnbuNWnUSNKh2aBeyvVIArVrA1mwuTILSCqDXqkE7oh4Auh7cMjyg0pIcl5CaslGhb8yLf4cXpcaGvfZmKyXmqr1XMFUwnefZ7Pm4sgomOsQzVzAddF4nBs-F7fV-ILGFZyaRI-FfSgJjDHyULBLF58OzxSOLEoRL_CKxhihwpcOhwCxs2HcuhUjYDTldJCZxv6t_UqvfdTIunuw9566vtFx3ZP_pW34c8GXgfwAAAP__es10TA). Burrows announced the assignments on the 31st day of the session, [tying the record](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx0kD1vhSAYhX8Nbhh4xQ8Ghi5st2tHg_CipChG6NX77xtv0rHzk_Ock_P1GB8mxLDNn2ZFVS6fRmDQUgaUi9GZEF-jqJyamJO8QsX7RrZNJ9hQLapvnfVTY5yxAhsvW5yY76WVKAfLWlsFdcsYcMEBesFrY6URA0DXg_PDBEQwdKGkoy4LFrxM9vGVnnjUNq1VVEspeybNBwFNQJ_nWX9nU25IQG94ZgL6HSOg7yoCmgEBzZs_QJf0k5HatK6hFERqcg7ztuJWMsWr4Obonk48aPIUrx2PgJtFR-e004jG4XHLq0O5_Qwxhtz1RLB5NSG-R5Z_X3sq-A0AAP__S75wvQ) for the longest delay in doing so over the last 30 years. Following the announcement and the passage of several congratulatory resolutions, the House adjourned until next Tuesday, continuing its month-long trend of taking 5-day weekends.

In April 2023, an entity named Rook TX purchased tickets for nearly every one of the [25.8 million 6-number combinations](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx00L2OwyAQBOCnsTssWPBfQXFNulx7pbWBdbISDhbsJfHbn5L-2tHo02h-zssZOfH9-o0beXmteQENvdKgjFsicjoW10Z_0XE2LXkz2rm3g9NTe_PTYGDUVgdNfQh2oB7QzrhO4GLvXN-yf2MajDMAozMdhhndBDCMENfpAo3TFFly6eRGQi-sazryg0oX8tYmfxPZa2O_Gjg1cLrTs3bPXFIMWPmeIxcKksvxbjdw-gAqZREqh1oL_kYVEvJW1V7ytotKdOWaUPhB7-hCypgRjG2Lj_uTU-I6jI3T1w05fTbIv6c8PPwFAAD__05PZho), ensuring a win of the $95 million jackpot. The purchases were processed by Lottery.com, an authorization granted by former executive director Gary Grief in contravention of the Texas Lottery's legislative intent. Although current executive director Ryan Mindell claimed the agency had updated its policies to ensure a similar scheme doesn’t occur again, senators were alarmed at Mindell’s [refusal to characterize](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx0kLtyqzAQhp9GdGKkRdwKFaeh82lTMoskbMULImhj7LfP4CZV2v82_3wfl_GCkeJ6_Y9LsPyc0wgKaqlAajN6jPQaTeHtpHyvi2B1W_V11RjVFTdrTGUM6rluwdfTrHVVV6puGjdh3wXdFtGeYwq00QCt0SW6Hk0H0LTg524CYVTwkdNe8i1weGKe6ZUeYS9dWgqyN-Yti-qfgEHAcBxHeX_iepoChjUcWcDwrsktUeTofgVKzEl-ortvieXXd8gc05olBfSS8FjwHvYsOUmHRHJOu0R3RgQMxW79dkSimJtWGHVdMNL7Ev_J6GHhJwAA__8u6mss) the incident as money laundering. “ _We just need to call in the Texas Rangers immediately_ ,” said Sen. Lois Kolkhorst (R-Brenham). Senators also grilled Mindell over two $50,000 payouts to a Lottery.com executive and the sale of a $1 million ticket to an anonymous buyer in China. According to state law, Texas Lottery winners must reside in the state, but the winning ticket was paid out two weeks after the 180-day deadline for cashing it in. “ _We can’t gloss over this; we can’t look the other way_ ,” said Sen. Paul Bettencourt (R-Houston).
## Homestead Exemption Increase Passes Senate
The Texas Senate unanimously passed legislation Thursday to [increase the homestead exemption](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx0kLGSrCAURL8GMiy4IGpA8BKzeemG1nW4jtSiWMKq8_dbTr5RJ92nus7XY3hgiGF9_ceFXLmmNICEWkgQygweQ3wPhns3St8pTk41uqu1NbLls9NU-7ptG0_a1kiapDTaKzQ0WUVjx4O7YRKUUQCNURU-OzQtgG3AT-0IzEjyoaS9KjMVujBP8Z0O2qtnWnh0cylbZvofg55Bf55nNaUL7Jx-cknrXWLQr3RmBv1nLjKtWOgOn4Uy8lvMaaFcCL2gi5athLSKMcQobgoJ3LY9HRj57vx2hhhDtg0z8rVgiJ8b5U8vh4PfAAAA___Nw2ea) from $100,000 ($110,000 for seniors) to $140,000 ($150,000) for seniors. body:
Please read the following message from our sponsor.
* * *

| The reason you wake up with that tightness in your chest is because of anxiety still lingering from the day before.

Sometimes the anxiety from many days before.

It all piles up until there's so much anxiety, you feel it even before you wake up.

It's called Overnight Anxiety because it sneak up on us while we sleep.

Thing about overnight anxiety is therapy can't help. Because we can't have therapy sessions in our sleep.

Here's what has to happen: the anxiety has to go away during the day so it doesn't wake you up in the night.

That's why microdosing magic mushrooms is so helpful for people suffering from overnight anxiety.

Because the magic mushrooms get rid of the anxiety in the brain. It's like the psilocybin absorbs the anxiety and turns it into a feeling of energy and positivity.

Throughout the day, you feel confident to do whatever is asked of you.

So you go to bed feeling at peace and wake up feeling refreshed.

Hi Friend,
Happy New Year! I hope the new year is starting off well for you and yours. I know that things are tough for so many of us right now, and for many, there is deep fear about darker times ahead.
Now, more than ever we have to do what we can to stand up for our own communities, and for members of communities who may be targeted over the next four years.
With that in mind, I am excited to tell you that I am continuing the fight as the PA Director of CASA. Since 2016, CASA has been advocating for policies that deliver justice for immigrants and Latino communities, the same communities that find themselves in the crosshairs of the new Administration. You can learn more about CASA by visiting their website wearecasa.org/Pennsylvania [http://wearecases.org/Pennsylvania] .
I’m fighting because the biggest concerns our children should have are fishing, coloring, and being kids. Instead too many are worried that their loved ones, their classmates, or even their parents may just disappear. I hope you will join me in supporting this important work at such a critical time.
As I embark on this next chapter, I am also asking for your help one more time. My campaign for Congress has some unpaid debts, and I really want to close out my committee to devote my full attention to the task at hand. You can help me do so by making a contribution one more time.
Click here to donate now! [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sdemail2023]
Thank you so much for your support over the past few years. I look forward to continuing to fight the good fight together!
With my best wishes!
Shamaine

Life-long liberal Jon Stewart **[made Biden's Deputy Secretary of Defense Kathleen Hicks PANIC](https://substack.com/redirect/bc1bf0df-b101-4c61-b3f1-1d815ee453df?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** when he pressed her on the unbelievable waste and loss of tax dollars by the Pentagon, during an off script live interview.

[Watch Video](https://substack.com/redirect/bc1bf0df-b101-4c61-b3f1-1d815ee453df?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

Hicks tried to laugh it off and shake her head, and her condescending reactions tell you everything you need to know about the government's attitude when the press and the public try to hold them accountable.

Friends,
The State Freedom Caucus Network has grown rapidly over the last three years, so we thought it would be a good idea to introduce ourselves to all our new supporters and followers. If you missed our last eight emails, we did a short Q&A with:
1. [Network President Andy Roth](https://substack.com/redirect/7bf0408a-8dcb-49b1-a530-62f904b98df7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
2. [Senior Vice President Justin Ouimette](https://substack.com/redirect/4ef136a5-0f02-447e-82ef-41d4182585c5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
3. [VP of Development Dana Craycroft and Sr. Development Director Sara Prinzi](https://substack.com/redirect/9f9ef7ea-eeb8-4412-b4a6-d7e021b31507?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
4. [VP of Government Affairs Cesar Ybarra](https://substack.com/redirect/711046b6-841c-45c4-b4ef-a8192748053d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
5. [State Directors Connie Hair (LA) and Nathan Dahm (OK)](https://substack.com/redirect/3b8af824-6ce3-4cad-a29f-3f77b606398d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
6. [State Directors Collin Moseley (IL) and Tim Jones (MO)](https://substack.com/redirect/68f5005e-4b50-45bd-adf7-93c72e0c863f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
7. [State Directors Jessie Rubino (WY) and Darin Gaub (MT)](https://substack.com/redirect/03c83d91-5377-4085-9851-e90ec3e2c100?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
8. [State Directors Evan Newman (SC) and Ali Rak (MD)](https://substack.com/redirect/87d1c8b7-e564-4768-bb6f-3f0ec0b797e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

This week are two more of our amazing state directors representing Arizona (**Suanne Edmiston**) and South Dakota (**Hannah Determan**).
Two interesting facts about them - Suanne is always in learning mode and even keeps a list of new hobbies she'd like to try, and then pursue them when there's the opportunity. Hannah graduated from South Dakota State University in May 2024 with a degree in Economics.
* * *
**SUANNE EDMISTON**
**What is your role at SFCN?** I am the State Director in Arizona for SFCN.
**Where are you from originally? Where do you live now?** I'm originally from New Wilmington, Pennsylvania, and I currently live in Phoenix, Arizona.
**Tell us about your family! And pets!** I am the fourth of four daughters. Much of my family, including my parents, still live in western Pennsylvania and the surrounding area. I now have a cat, but it's more accurate to say that he adopted me. His name is Mordecai. He ran up to me in my parking lot about 6 months after moving to Phoenix. I definitely had no intention of getting a pet, but every evening I'd go outside to see if he was around, and he usually was. That went on for about a month and when I decided to take him to the vet to see what the situation was, the vet basically said that I was his new owner, declaring "one man's trash is another man's treasure." The whole thing was actually pretty odd, but he is definitely a treasure!
**What's the best part of your job?** There are many wonderful aspects, but I think the best part is using my skillset to provide reinforcement to the dedicated, smart and principled members I get to work with on a daily basis. I fully appreciate that government service is not easy when your motivations are correct and your principles resolute. And yet, there are so many forces trying to tear you from that principled path. I enjoy being able to provide whatever I can - research, analysis, facts, data, recommendations - to oppose the corrupting forces of "consensus" (often cronyism, more accurately) at any cost.
**How did you come to SFCN? What did you do before?** Prior to SFCN, I served on Capitol Hill for almost 11 years. During those years, I worked for three House members, starting in my home district (now PA-16), and then the fourth district of Iowa and the first district of Texas. I was blessed with wonderful bosses, colleagues, and constituents, which made the hard slog in the Swamp manageable. Overall, it was a wonderful experience and training, learning from those who battled the swamp daily and tirelessly for many years to keep their constituents as the reason for being. Connie Hair, current State Director in Louisiana, was my Chief of Staff in Congressman Louie Gohmert's office. Connie knew the State Director in Arizona was an open position, and connected me to Andy and Justin. That was over two years ago now, and it's been an adventure and privilege to serve in this new and exciting capacity fighting for freedom in Arizona.
**Who or what most shaped your political philosophy/ideology?** This is really hard, because there have been so many. My parents and extended family definitely formed the foundation. The news, talk radio and lively "debate" was and remains on a loop in my parental home. I'm grateful that I had the principle of intellectual freedom ingrained very early, because I think it allowed me to pursue learning with curiosity, to find the valuable in every source while not feeling the need to accept any one source's position in totality. With time, I find myself looking more and more toward Jesus in all things. In our work, I think often about how the Lord is such a gentleman, that he does not impose himself on his own creation. I think there's a strong message to be extracted from that truth that is highly relevant in many aspects of life, including human government: just because a government can impose itself, doesn't mean it should. I also find Thomas Acquinas very helpful in his commentary on the law and how we make ethical decisions concerning it. I studied him many years ago, but his wisdom is often echoing in my head as I read, review, analyze and assess legislation.
***Pick One To Answer*: Favorite food? Favorite place to vacation? Favorite Book? Favorite Quote?** There's so many, but I'll pick a quote that I think is very grounding, maybe even especially so in our times: "Let your credo be this: Let the lie come into the world, let it even triumph. But not through me". - Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6cb149ee-f8a4-4029-82b7-79a3dbe06822?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* * *
**HANNAH DETERMAN**
**What is your role at SFCN?** I'm the South Dakota State Director! I work to advance liberty in the state by working with Freedom Caucus members and other conservative legislators.
**Where are you from originally? Where do you live now?** I'm originally from Minnesota but have spent the last few years in Oklahoma. Now, I'm settling into South Dakota!
**Tell us about your family! And pets!** I have two younger siblings--my brother is in college, and my sister is a high school junior. My dog, Aspen, is seven years old and is living with my family in Oklahoma. I also got engaged to my fiance, Zach, ten months ago! We've been together for three years and are getting married in September.
**What's the best part of your job?** I love the hustle of legislative advocacy at the Capitol and working alongside Freedom Caucus legislators.
**How did you come to SFCN? What did you do before?** A connection in South Dakota referred me to SFCN. Before that, I worked at Young Americans for Liberty as a Deputy Regional Director.
**Who or what most shaped your political philosophy/ideology?** My faith defines my politics. I was also raised in a conservative household--my mom was politically active in grassroots when I was growing up, and my dad always has The Blaze TV on at home! My time at Young Americans for Liberty also introduced me to incredible mentors who further shaped my philosophy.
***Pick One To Answer*: Favorite food? Favorite place to vacation? Favorite Book? Favorite Quote?** My favorite vacation has always been visiting family in Oklahoma!

If you missed our last eight emails, we did a short Q&A with: 1. 2. 3. 4. 5. 6. 7. 8. This week are two more of our amazing state directors representing Arizona (Suanne Edmiston) and South Dakota (Hannah Determan). Two interesting facts about them - Suanne is always in learning mode and even keeps a list of new hobbies she'd like to try, and then pursue them when there's the opportunity. Hannah graduated from South Dakota State University in May 2024 with a degree in Economics. SUANNE EDMISTON What is your role at SFCN? I am the State Director in Arizona for SFCN. Where are you from originally? Where do you live now? I'm originally from New Wilmington, Pennsylvania, and I currently live in Phoenix, Arizona. Tell us about your family! And pets! I am the fourth of four daughters. Much of my family, including my parents, still live in western Pennsylvania and the surrounding area. I now have a cat, but it's more accurate to say that he adopted me. His name is Mordecai. He ran up to me in my parking lot about 6 months after moving to Phoenix. I definitely had no intention of getting a pet, but every evening I'd go outside to see if he was around, and he usually was. That went on for about a month and when I decided to take him to the vet to see what the situation was, the vet basically said that I was his new owner, declaring "one man's trash is another man's treasure." The whole thing was actually pretty odd, but he is definitely a treasure! What's the best part of your job? There are many wonderful aspects, but I think the best part is using my skillset to provide reinforcement to the dedicated, smart and principled members I get to work with on a daily basis. I fully appreciate that government service is not easy when your motivations are correct and your principles resolute. And yet, there are so many forces trying to tear you from that principled path. I enjoy being able to provide whatever I can - research, analysis, facts, data, recommendations - to oppose the corrupting forces of "consensus" (often cronyism, more accurately) at any cost. How did you come to SFCN? What did you do before? Prior to SFCN, I served on Capitol Hill for almost 11 years. During those years, I worked for three House members, starting in my home district (now PA-16), and then the fourth district of Iowa and the first district of Texas. I was blessed with wonderful bosses, colleagues, and constituents, which made the hard slog in the Swamp manageable. Overall, it was a wonderful experience and training, learning from those who battled the swamp daily and tirelessly for many years to keep their constituents as the reason for being. Connie Hair, current State Director in Louisiana, was my Chief of Staff in Congressman Louie Gohmert's office. Connie knew the State Director in Arizona was an open position, and connected me to Andy and Justin. That was over two years ago now, and it's been an adventure and privilege to serve in this new and exciting capacity fighting for freedom in Arizona. Who or what most shaped your political philosophy/ideology? This is really hard, because there have been so many. My parents and extended family definitely formed the foundation. The news, talk radio and lively "debate" was and remains on a loop in my parental home. I'm grateful that I had the principle of intellectual freedom ingrained very early, because I think it allowed me to pursue learning with curiosity, to find the valuable in every source while not feeling the need to accept any one source's position in totality. With time, I find myself looking more and more toward Jesus in all things. In our work, I think often about how the Lord is such a gentleman, that he does not impose himself on his own creation. I think there's a strong message to be extracted from that truth that is highly relevant in many aspects of life, including human government: just because a government can impose itself, doesn't mean it should. I also find Thomas Acquinas very helpful in his commentary on the law and how we make ethical decisions concerning it. I studied him many years ago, but his wisdom is often echoing in my head as I read, review, analyze and assess legislation. Pick One To Answer: Favorite food? Favorite place to vacation? Favorite Book? Favorite Quote? There's so many, but I'll pick a quote that I think is very grounding, maybe even especially so in our times: "Let your credo be this: Let the lie come into the world, let it even triumph. But not through me". - Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn | | ---|---|--- HANNAH DETERMAN What is your role at SFCN? I'm the South Dakota State Director! I work to advance liberty in the state by working with Freedom Caucus members and other conservative legislators. Where are you from originally? Where do you live now? I'm originally from Minnesota but have spent the last few years in Oklahoma. Now, I'm settling into South Dakota! Tell us about your family! And pets! I have two younger siblings--my brother is in college, and my sister is a high school junior. My dog, Aspen, is seven years old and is living with my family in Oklahoma. I also got engaged to my fiance, Zach, ten months ago! We've been together for three years and are getting married in September. What's the best part of your job? I love the hustle of legislative advocacy at the Capitol and working alongside Freedom Caucus legislators. How did you come to SFCN? What did you do before? A connection in South Dakota referred me to SFCN. Before that, I worked at Young Americans for Liberty as a Deputy Regional Director. Who or what most shaped your political philosophy/ideology? My faith defines my politics. I was also raised in a conservative household--my mom was politically active in grassroots when I was growing up, and my dad always has The Blaze TV on at home! My time at Young Americans for Liberty also introduced me to incredible mentors who further shaped my philosophy. *Pick One To Answer: Favorite food? Favorite place to vacation? Favorite Book? body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/EA/EA016/1/99735/images/NPP_Ed_logo_RGB_green1-01.jpg]
Hi Friend,
Welcome to the latest New PA Project Education Fund (NPPEF) newsletter!
We are happy to report that Pennsylvania has seen a sharp decline in mail ballot rejections. [https://www.abc27.com/pennsylvania-politics/pennsylvania-reports-sharp-decline-in-mail-ballot-rejections/]
We are excited to continue our vital work providing civic education to our centered communities.
As a voting rights organization, our mission is to provide current, accurate, and accessible information about the importance of voting in every election.
Thank you for doing your part to stay informed and engaged!
Social Media of the Week
https://www.instagram.com/p/DC0QUXzBMPe/ [https://www.instagram.com/p/DC0QUXzBMPe/]
Before the country gets ready for the beginning of Black History Month, we want to highlight this video post from Vintage & Iconic African American Everything.
By watching it, you can learn a little about the hidden messages conveyed through quilts during the Underground Railroad, the secret network that helped enslaved people escape to freedom between 1820 and 1861.
SHARE ON INSTAGRAM [https://www.instagram.com/p/DC0QUXzBMPe/]
The right to vote has been undercut across the country and remains at risk—especially for Black voters and other voters of color.
Instead of strengthening these protections by enacting the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act, leadership in Congress is pushing anti-voter legislation that will add more barriers to the ballot.
As Black voters and other voters of color across the country face the greatest assault on their voting rights since the Jim Crow era, a growing number of states are acting to protect the right to vote and safeguard our democracy.
With the passage of State Voting Rights Acts, states can provide key protections to their constituents that prevent and guard against discriminatory voting practices and policies.
Message or call [https://www.legis.state.pa.us/cfdocs/legis/home/member_information/mbrList.cfm?body=H] your representatives to let them know you want a State Voting Rights Act in Pennsylvania.
Do not forget to make sure your right to vote is still intact.
#YourPowerYourVoiceYourVote
CHECK YOUR REGISTRATION STATUS [https://vote.pa/?org=nppef]
RECENT EVENTS
[https://d15k2d11r6t6rl.cloudfront.net/public/users/Integrators/04eaa6b2-88f4-43b4-b978-7bb0708f5838/572F74527141787142367832646E2B79766B6F4869435068772F646E5867485352734D656F342F394551326D7A49364762424A38585256527431734E59542B4E/editor_images/WCM201%20yellow%20town%20hall%20SQUARE%20GRAPHIC_mallet_2.png] On Thursday, January 30th from 6:30 to 8:00PM , Why Courts Matter - Pennsylvania and affiliated organization New Pennsylvania Project hosted their second virtual town hall on the importance of our state and federal courts.
The very interactive town hall helped attendees understand more about what the courts are doing to protect their rights, as well as the process to retain a judge.
WATCH THE RECORDING [https://www.facebook.com/NewPennsylvaniaProject/videos/988292736687812]
[https://d15k2d11r6t6rl.cloudfront.net/public/users/Integrators/04eaa6b2-88f4-43b4-b978-7bb0708f5838/7237344C447445787878394747342B75584E47375A57552F745265427662334B544A4A36505A58657A5871474B7A5A6E53705571424758325657365969365747/editor_images/WCM%20logo.JPG] #CourtsMatter
[https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/trumps-bid-expand-presidential-power-hits-first-snag-politics-desk-rcna189050] [https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/trumps-bid-expand-presidential-power-hits-first-snag-politics-desk-rcna189050] [https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/trumps-bid-expand-presidential-power-hits-first-snag-politics-desk-rcna189050] [https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/trumps-bid-expand-presidential-power-hits-first-snag-politics-desk-rcna189050] [https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/trumps-bid-expand-presidential-power-hits-first-snag-politics-desk-rcna189050] [https://www.democracydocket.com/analysis/4-voting-rights-cases-scotus-may-hear-that-could-reshape-elections/] Trump's bid to expand presidential power hits its first snag: From the Politics Desk [https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/trumps-bid-expand-presidential-power-hits-first-snag-politics-desk-rcna189050]
" It took all of three days for a judge to say one of President Donald Trump’s executive orders is “blatantly unconstitutional.” The order in question seeks to deny citizenship to children born in the United States whose parents are not citizens or lawful residents."
Trump administration rescinds funding freeze ahead of court hearing [https://www.reuters.com/legal/white-house-set-fight-court-after-judge-pauses-trumps-funding-freeze-2025-01-29/]
"The Trump administration on Wednesday rescinded a sweeping directive to pause federal loans, grants and other financial assistance, a White House official said, just shortly before it was set to appear in court for a second straight day to defend the policy."
Appellate Court Revives New York Voting Rights Act [https://www.democracydocket.com/news-alerts/new-york-judge-strikes-down-states-voting-rights-act/]
"An appellate court in New York reversed [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/2025-01-30-Opinion.pdf] a lower court overturning the state’s John R. Lewis Voting Rights Act (NYVRA) — a law that grants voters additional protections not covered by federal law.The four-judge panel ruled unanimously that Newburgh, New York, failed to show how remedying vote dilution in accordance with the NYVRA would violate the 14th Amendment’s Equal Protection Clause."
News You Can Use
PA House approves bills that would codify Affordable Care Act protections in state law [https://www.cityandstatepa.com/policy/2024/10/pa-house-approves-bills-would-codify-affordable-care-act-protections-state-law/400172/]
" Lawmakers in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives on Wednesday approved a series of bills that would enshrine protections outlined in the federal Affordable Care Act into state law in the event that former President Barack Obama’s signature health care law is repealed or invalidated at the federal level. "
Pennsylvanians Deserve Fair Maps [https://www.commoncause.org/pennsylvania/press/pennsylvanians-deserve-fair-maps/]
"Common Cause is advocating for an end to political gerrymandering with fair redistricting laws in Pennsylvania. This legislation would update the state’s constitution and implement an independent citizens redistricting commission to draw state legislative and congressional districts."
Trump’s Executive Order Freezing Federal Payments is Harmful, Illegal and Unconstitutional [https://pennpolicy.org/penn-policy-center-statement-on-pres-trumps-executive-order-freezing-federal-payments-to-state-and-local-governments-and-social-service-providers/?nvep=&hmac=&emci=55284ace-65de-ef11-88f8-0022482a9579&emdi=ea000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001&ceid=]
[https://www.votebeat.org/2025/01/13/2025-voting-elections-noncitizen-state-legislatures/] "Late on Monday, the Trump administration issued an executive order halting payment of grants and loans to state and local governments, social service providers, and others. This action is illegal and unconstitutional. And it is likely to cause immediate and widespread harm to people and families across our state and the country. It must be rescinded by the President as soon as possible."
NPPEF on the ground
Pennsylvanians have a lot of questions regarding the many confusing executive orders they're seeing on the news. We expect this to be the case for the next few months.
Our teams are ready to help break the cycle of misinformation spread, and make sure registered voters have the facts.
When you see our teams on the ground, even if you are registered to vote, approach us to get some civic education.
Lancaster County

clean_body: [] Hi Friend, Welcome to the latest New PA Project Education Fund (NPPEF) newsletter! We are happy to report that Pennsylvania has seen a sharp decline in mail ballot rejections. [] We are excited to continue our vital work providing civic education to our centered communities. As a voting rights organization, our mission is to provide current, accurate, and accessible information about the importance of voting in every election. Thank you for doing your part to stay informed and engaged! Social Media of the Week [] Before the country gets ready for the beginning of Black History Month, we want to highlight this video post from Vintage & Iconic African American Everything. By watching it, you can learn a little about the hidden messages conveyed through quilts during the Underground Railroad, the secret network that helped enslaved people escape to freedom between 1820 and 1861. SHARE ON INSTAGRAM [] The right to vote has been undercut across the country and remains at risk—especially for Black voters and other voters of color. Instead of strengthening these protections by enacting the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act, leadership in Congress is pushing anti-voter legislation that will add more barriers to the ballot. As Black voters and other voters of color across the country face the greatest assault on their voting rights since the Jim Crow era, a growing number of states are acting to protect the right to vote and safeguard our democracy. With the passage of State Voting Rights Acts, states can provide key protections to their constituents that prevent and guard against discriminatory voting practices and policies. Message or call [] your representatives to let them know you want a State Voting Rights Act in Pennsylvania. Do not forget to make sure your right to vote is still intact. #YourPowerYourVoiceYourVote CHECK YOUR REGISTRATION STATUS [] RECENT EVENTS [] On Thursday, January 30th from 6:30 to 8:00PM , Why Courts Matter - Pennsylvania and affiliated organization New Pennsylvania Project hosted their second virtual town hall on the importance of our state and federal courts. The very interactive town hall helped attendees understand more about what the courts are doing to protect their rights, as well as the process to retain a judge. WATCH THE RECORDING [] [] #CourtsMatter [] [] [] [] [] [] Trump's bid to expand presidential power hits its first snag: From the Politics Desk [] " It took all of three days for a judge to say one of President Donald Trump’s executive orders is “blatantly unconstitutional.” The order in question seeks to deny citizenship to children born in the United States whose parents are not citizens or lawful residents." Trump administration rescinds funding freeze ahead of court hearing [] "The Trump administration on Wednesday rescinded a sweeping directive to pause federal loans, grants and other financial assistance, a White House official said, just shortly before it was set to appear in court for a second straight day to defend the policy." Appellate Court Revives New York Voting Rights Act [] "An appellate court in New York reversed [] a lower court overturning the state’s John R. Lewis Voting Rights Act (NYVRA) — a law that grants voters additional protections not covered by federal law.The four-judge panel ruled unanimously that Newburgh, New York, failed to show how remedying vote dilution in accordance with the NYVRA would violate the 14th Amendment’s Equal Protection Clause." News You Can Use PA House approves bills that would codify Affordable Care Act protections in state law [] " Lawmakers in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives on Wednesday approved a series of bills that would enshrine protections outlined in the federal Affordable Care Act into state law in the event that former President Barack Obama’s signature health care law is repealed or invalidated at the federal level. " Pennsylvanians Deserve Fair Maps [] "Common Cause is advocating for an end to political gerrymandering with fair redistricting laws in Pennsylvania. This legislation would update the state’s constitution and implement an independent citizens redistricting commission to draw state legislative and congressional districts." Trump’s Executive Order Freezing Federal Payments is Harmful, Illegal and Unconstitutional [=] [] "Late on Monday, the Trump administration issued an executive order halting payment of grants and loans to state and local governments, social service providers, and others. This action is illegal and unconstitutional. And it is likely to cause immediate and widespread harm to people and families across our state and the country. It must be rescinded by the President as soon as possible." NPPEF on the ground Pennsylvanians have a lot of questions regarding the many confusing executive orders they're seeing on the news. We expect this to be the case for the next few months. Our teams are ready to help break the cycle of misinformation spread, and make sure registered voters have the facts. name: PoliticsPA
subject: How accurate were the 2024 polls?
body:
Tune into the latest installment of the Voices of Reason podcast. | | | |
---
| | | Welcome to the latest edition of _Voices of Reason_ where we’ll recap exclusive news and data featured in our most recent podcast.

Did the experts get it right? We're looking back at the bold predictions made ahead of the 2024 election to see how they stacked up with the surprising outcomes.

Eagle Consulting Group's **Chris Nicholas** and** ** Real Clear PA's **Charles McElwee **share insights you don’t want to miss.
---
| **Big Names Make News**
---
| **Principal of Eagle Consulting Group Chris Nicholas** examined how the GOP coalition is “reorganizing along socioeconomic levels ” while Democrats are “struggling with an age shift as younger, progressive members” join their ranks. [[Watch](https://broadandliberty.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=f64f3463dd&e=b7b3eddce2)]

**Founding Editor of Real Clear PA Charles McElwee** explained that doctors, once reliably Republican, now lean Left as "younger, transient" professionals favor higher-paying employee roles over owning risky small practices. [[Watch](https://broadandliberty.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=eba63abd54&e=b7b3eddce2)]
---
|
* * *
---
| **Numbers You Need to Know**
---
| _Election Polling_
* **6 in 10** polling sites predicted a Harris win, **3 in 10** predicted a Trump win, and 1 called a tie. [[FiveThirtyEight](https://broadandliberty.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=e2f19e4c88&e=b7b3eddce2)]
* Predictive polls showed Harris leading **79% to 17%** among PA Black voters, down from Biden's **92% to 7%** advantage in 2020. [[ABC](https://broadandliberty.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=82a8c345b9&e=b7b3eddce2)]

_Gender Breakdown_
* A large gender gap was predicted, with young women favoring Harris by **17 points** and young men preferring Trump by **14 points**. [[TuffsCircle](https://broadandliberty.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=dd7d94882a&e=b7b3eddce2)]
* Democrats were anticipating to lose support among voters, especially **men under 30**, particularly in Midwest states. [[NPR](https://broadandliberty.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=942117946f&e=b7b3eddce2)]

---
|

---

realignment before it happened**
---
| [ ](https://broadandliberty.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=0d3a9a8c56&e=b7b3eddce2 "Why Joe Biden is in PA Every Other Week | Voices of Reason Ep. 3")
---
|
* * *
---
| **In Case You Missed It...**
---
| The _Voices of Reason_ podcast has covered the most important issues in Pennsylvania politics – from [education funding](https://broadandliberty.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=56572ef5df&e=b7b3eddce2) to [trust in elections](https://broadandliberty.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=f0ab1ae7ac&e=b7b3eddce2). Secretary of the Commonwealth [Al Schmidt](https://broadandliberty.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=913c30dde8&e=b7b3eddce2), PA Treasurer [Stacy Garrity](https://broadandliberty.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=0d15ea87d2&e=b7b3eddce2), and House Appropriations Chairman [Jordan Harris](https://broadandliberty.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=e1242c31b1&e=b7b3eddce2) are just a few of many influential guests who have joined us for exclusive interviews and roundtable discussions.

name: New PA Project Education Fund
subject: Invest in accurate and accessible educational resources
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the New PA Project Education Fund
body:
Fellow activist,

As the Trump administration works to instill fear into our immigrant communities, we are doing everything we can to provide support and civic education about people’s rights. In this time of so much mis and dis-information, it is critical to provide factual, accurate and accessible educational resources to all.

The New PA Project Education Fund is currently working on developing educational resources in both English and Spanish to be distributed on the ground when engaging in conversations with Pennsylvanians. One example that is in production is a “Know Your Rights” informational card that will describe the constitutional rights a person has and what to do if/when they are faced with an ICE agent. With your support, we will be able to create, print and distribute these throughout our centered communities across PA. Will you help fund this project?

Here is an example of what the cards will look like:

You have constitutional rights:
- DO NOT OPEN THE DOOR if an immigration agent is knocking on the door.
- DO NOT ANSWER ANY QUESTIONS from an immigration agent if he or she tries to talk to you. You have the right to remain silent.
- DO NOT SIGN ANYTHING without first talking to a lawyer. You have the right to speak to a lawyer.
- If you are outside your home, ask the officer if you are free to leave and if he or she says yes, leave quietly.
- GIVE THIS CARD TO THE OFFICER. If you are inside your home, show the card out the window or slip it under the door.

Our thoughts are with immigrant communities as Trump deploys ICE to terrorize our neighbors across the country. 31 states have agreed to accept this permit so far. That’s because it’s simply the closest and easiest path to a semi-nationally recognized permit that’s available right now.

This permit isn’t just a basic concealed carry permit either. **It’s one of a kind... and is available to you No Matter what state you reside in.**

**Hurry and get it now.**

**[There are no guarantees this website](https://links.nationalgunowner.org/a/1537/click/20298/6374453/250aa762bb2e69b55e7bb2f43fd982c5b5610fb2/b4aa6158ce49adcb4bd9af7c9474bd6b05425259)** will be able to legally deliver this certificate to your email address after today!

Great news!

My [Anti-SLAPP bill](https://substack.com/redirect/d2baa4a3-7f19-495c-bd16-fdfd553a2d34?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) cruised through the House committee this week with zero opposition. Next stop: the House floor, where it'll pass, and the Governor will seal the deal.
_Protection from "lawfare" is coming to Idaho._
The bill is designed to deter an abusive type of litigation called a "SLAPP," or "strategic lawsuit against public participation." SLAPPs pose a grave threat to free speech, because they're not deisgend to "win," but to _**intimidate, distract, bankrupt, or punish**_.
Defending against these lawsuits can span years and drain tens of thousands of dollars.
In response, my proposed free speech protection bill lays out a comprehensive and efficient strategy for swiftly resolving these baseless legal attacks, safeguarding our fundamental right to free speech from undue and unjust challenges.

Friends,
In the past, I’ve been a vocal supporter of the freedom of the global press. In 2021, I introduced bipartisan legislation with Senator Lindsey Graham — the International Press Freedom Act — that would take measures to protect journalists around the world and those seeking refuge in the U.S. Last year, I co-sponsored a resolution recognizing the importance of press freedom and highlighting the growing threats to that freedom worldwide. These are critical issues and ones I’m proud to advocate for in the Senate.
Right now, we need to turn our attention to the freedom of the press here at home.
It’s in the First Amendment of the U.S. Constitution, and a cornerstone of our democracy — the government cannot and must not interfere with the publishing and reporting of information to the American people.
Court cases have backed up and indeed strengthened press protections over the years, helping to protect against corruption and abuse of power and to allow the public to make informed decisions.
But this week, the Trump Administration actually barred an Associated Press journalist from accessing an Oval Office event as punishment for not updating their editorial guide to reflect Trump’s name change of the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America:
https://secure.ngpvan.com/Mpyltbog4UShPXQUTe4GTw2 [https://secure.ngpvan.com/Mpyltbog4UShPXQUTe4GTw2]
This may be the first egregious action against the freedom of the press from the Trump Administration, but we can be sure that it won’t be the last.
I’m asking for your support today: Add your name to my petition to demand that we maintain a free press as dictated by the Constitution. [https://secure.ngpvan.com/Mpyltbog4UShPXQUTe4GTw2]
I strongly denounce the Administration’s decision to punish the AP and its journalists by revoking access, and I will do whatever I can to protect the freedom of the press.
A strong public showing helps — so please, sign on today to say you will fight for the freedom of the press with me. [https://secure.ngpvan.com/Mpyltbog4UShPXQUTe4GTw2]
Thanks for reading, and more to come.
-Tim Kaine

clean_body: | | | Right off the bat, Peter, let me say THANK YOU. You may not know this, but I can only count on about 30% of conservatives to even open my emails, so you've already gone above and beyond for me. Can I ask you for one more favor, though? I'm humbly asking you to read this email all the way through. It'll only take a minute, and if you still think your dollar doesn't matter, then I'll simply thank you for your time. In addition to only 30% of folks opening this email, only 1-2% will take the extra step to donate. Unfortunately, conservatives in tough races like me rely on emails and letters like this to hit our fundraising goals. I can't call up woke CEOs or well-connected millionaires to stroke a million-dollar check to hit my goal. I count on America-loving patriots like you who donate a few bucks when you can afford it. Look, we won BIG in 2024, but with President Trump in the White House, Democrats are chomping at the bit to exact their revenge against House Republicans like me who are going to help him secure our border, cut taxes, and Make America Great Again! Every little bit we can raise today will help stave off an impending Democrat takeover. Here 's my last request: Democrats have attacked my faith and my race already in order to win. They will do even worse this time around to defeat me. There's a reason Democrats consistently resort to dirty tactics to win. They don't just want to win... They want to DEMORALIZE us. Well, I've got news for them: I 'm not giving up on us. I 'm not giving up on our values. And I 'm counting on you to not give up on me. There are a lot of conservatives out there who will give up, but not you. You chose to open this email and hear me out. Together, under President Donald Trump, we will defend the American Dream I was lucky enough to live. Not just for my kids, but the entire next generation of kids in this country. If you are longing for the days when Joe Biden and Barack Obama were president, then I could see why you wouldn't step up and donate today. Thank you so much for just hearing me out. If you can't afford to donate today, just keep me in your prayers and remember me the next time you have a few dollars to spare.
